Walk. Spin. Go.

The concept is simple. A person walks up to a single panel, turns through a full rotation in front of it, and continues past. The turn captures the full body, so one panel does the work that otherwise takes a lane. It puts HEXWAVE in hallways, doorways, and other entrances where a multi-panel footprint was never practical.

“The I-Configuration gives security operators a new level of flexibility in how they design and implement their security screening operations without sacrificing detection capability,” said Bill Frain, CEO of Liberty Defense. “We listened to customers who wanted the breadth of detection that HEXWAVE provides but needed a solution that could fit into the physical constraints of their facilities. The I-Configuration is our response.”

The I-Configuration comes as prohibited item lists keep outgrowing what a metal detector was built to find. In a recent evaluation using the S-Configuration, HEXWAVE supported enforcement of a major sporting venue’s prohibited items list across approximately 2,000 people over three consecutive nights at a high-traffic public entrance. Supervisors reported people stepping out of line once they saw what was coming out of pockets, and others dropping items on the sidewalk rather than carrying them forward.
“What I didn’t expect was the supervisors pulling us aside to talk about the people who walked away before they ever got to us,” said Scott Brown, Senior Service Manager at Liberty Defense.

HEXWAVE uses millimeter wave technology and 3D video-rate imaging to detect metallic and non-metallic threats concealed on people, with automatic threat detection powered by AI and deep learning algorithms. It does not store images or capture personal information.

Liberty Defense will have the S-Configuration and the I-Configuration running at booth 4268 in Halls B1-B5. Security leaders can see the I-Configuration operate for the first time, talk through the evaluation findings on site, and schedule time at sales@libertydefense.com.
About Liberty Defense

Liberty Defense (NASDAQ: DETX; TSXV: SCAN) provides multi-technology security solutions for concealed weapons detection in high volume foot traffic areas and locations requiring enhanced security such as airports, stadiums, schools, and more. Liberty’s HEXWAVE product, for which the Company has secured an exclusive license from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), as well as a technology transfer agreement for patents related to active 3D radar imaging technology, provides discrete, modular, and scalable protection to provide layered, stand-off detection capability of metallic and non-metallic weapons. Liberty has also recently licensed the millimeter wave-based, High-Definition Advanced Imaging Technology (HD-AIT) body scanner and shoe scanner technologies as part of its technology portfolio. Liberty is committed to protecting communities and preserving peace of mind through superior security detection solutions.
